articles.title: Spanish Grand Prix: Antonelli holds off Verstappen to stretch F1 championship lead – live
articles.summary: Lights out at 2pm (all times BST) Ecclestone questioned after shotgun found on private jet Share your thoughts with John via email. The formation lap is away. It’s a hot day in Madrid, 31 degrees, no shade at all. The track temperature is 54 degrees.
body: Kimi Antonelli speaks: "Yeah, it was a very difficult race. not straightforward at all, especially trying to match tyres. But yeah, I think today, you know, it’s good to win, but it doesn’t feel as good because I think Lando today deserves to win. But overall, you know, we’ll take it.

Max Verstappen: “So, yeah, for us, I think today, P2 is an incredible result because you could see how much Lando is catching me, but around here you can’t pass. So I could keep him behind. It’s a challenging track. It’s challenging when you’re driving by yourself looking forward.

Lando Norris: “There was nothing I could do. Congrats to Kimi and Max. They drove a good race today. So just luck not on our side and I gave it a good, good fight to try and catch up with with Max, but it’s difficult to pass. The team are doing an amazing job. We’re working hard. We have to continue to work hard because these guys are doing a good job and it’s tough at the top. So yeah, we’ll keep pushing, keep trying. and more wins are possible so we’ll keep an eye up and then keep pushing.”

articles.title: Cristiano Ronaldo calls for lifetime bans in Saudi Pro League after Diogo Jota chants
articles.summary: Al-Hilal’s Rúben Neves subjected to chants at Al-Taawoun. Neves was close friend of Jota and pallbearer at funeral. Cristiano Ronaldo said that fans who appeared to ⁠make chants referencing his former teammate Diogo Jota at Rúben Neves during a Saudi ⁠Pro League ⁠match ​should be banned for life…
body: The chants occurred on Saturday during ⁠a fixture between Al-Taawoun and Neves’s side, Al-Hilal, in Buraydah, Saudi Arabia.
Jota died last year in a car crash in Zamora, ​north-western Spain, along with ‌his brother André ‌Silva. A close friend of Jota, Neves was a ‌pallbearer at his funeral.

Footage filmed from the stands during the match and circulated on social media appeared to show supporters chanting “Jota”. The shouts attracted the attention of Neves, who pointed to his eye and ‌then up to the sky in response. Passing through the mixed zone after the game, ​Neves said: “I hope they don’t go to pray afterwards.”
The game finished 6-0 to Al-Hilal, with Neves playing 75 minutes before being substituted.

articles.title: Antonelli wins as Norris loses out under virtual safety car
articles.summary: Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli wins the Spanish Grand Prix after McLaren's Lando Norris loses out because of the bad timing of a virtual safety car.
body: Norris was leading comfortably from pole position when the VSC was called on lap 15. The timing was terrible for the world champion - he had already passed the pit exit when the VSC was called.
That meant Antonelli and Verstappen were able to pit under the VSC, saving time, while the caution period ended before Norris could make it around to the pits again.
He did then come in but, to make matters worse, the stop was slow and he rejoined in fifth place.
Norris was able to recover only to third around this track where overtaking is next to impossible.

articles.title: Chelsea thrash Manchester United in WSL as Lauren James revels in free role
articles.summary: A swaggering Chelsea cast off any suggestion that they had lost the ability to kill off games, putting five goals past a worryingly lacklustre and lackadaisical Manchester United side.
body: The match had been talked about as something of a must win for Sonia Bompastor’s side after they were inexplicably held to a 1-1 draw by Aston Villa on the opening weekend, despite a staggering domination of that match. Criticism felt harsh given their level of control over the game, but signs of the profligacy evident last season reared its head in warning at Stamford Bridge.

To some extent the concern did not need to be too deep. Chelsea were at their creative best against Villa and were without the injured centre-forwards Melvine Malard and Mayra Ramírez, while Aggie Beever-Jones, who led the line against the Midlands side, had not scored in the Women’s Super League since September 2025. Off-target Beever-Jones was relegated to the bench for the trip to United. Instead, Lauren James and Sjoeke Nüsken worked away interchangeably up front.

The visitors were similarly fluid in other areas, lining up for kick-off in a back three, at times converting to a back four and at others seemingly playing with a back two. It was super effective. Chelsea were unpredictable and James’s free-to-roam role put their super-talent at the centre of everything.

articles.title: Ronaldo demands lifetime bans over Jota chants
articles.summary: Footage on social media appears to show Al-Hilal's Ruben Neves reacting to Al-Taawoun fans chanting Diogo Jota's name at him during their Saudi Pro League match.
body: Portugal star Cristiano Ronaldo has called for lifetime bans to be issued to fans who chanted the late Diogo Jota's name towards his international team-mate Ruben Neves.
Liverpool forward Jota died in a car crash at the age of 28 in July last year, and was a close friend of midfielder Neves, having played together for Wolverhampton Wanderers and Portugal.
Supporters appeared to target Al-Hilal midfielder Neves before his side's 6-0 win against Al-Taawoun in the Saudi Pro League on Saturday by repeatedly shouting "Jota" at him.
"The league must take action and punish this kind of fan behaviour," forward Ronaldo, who also plays in the Saudi league for Al-Nassr, wrote on social media.

articles.title: Rangers v Aberdeen & Edinburgh derby in League Cup semis
articles.summary: Rangers have been drawn against Aberdeen in the semi-finals of the Premier Sports Cup, while rivals Heart of Midlothian and Hibernian will face off in the other tie at Hampden Park.
body: The semi-final ties will take place at Hampden Park on the weekend of 31 October-1 November.
Derek McInnes' side reached the last four with a comprehensive victory over Celtic at Ibrox on Sunday, having last won this competition in the 2023-24 season when they beat Aberdeen 1-0 in the final.
In the other quarter-final matches, Hibernian beat League 1 Ross County 3-0, Hearts beat Stenhousemuir by the same score and Aberdeen knocked out Kilmarnock on penalties.
There has already been an Edinburgh derby this season, with Hearts winning 3-1 at Easter Road in the Scottish Premiership.

articles.title: World championship leader Antonelli wins Spanish GP
articles.summary: Kimi Antonelli extended his lead in the world championship with his eighth victory of the season at the Spanish Formula One Grand Prix at the Madring on Sunday. The 20-year-old Mercedes driver finished clear of Max Verstappen (Red Bull) and Lando Norris (McLaren) and is now 81 points ahead of…
body: Ferrari's Charles Leclerc (Ferrari) finished fourth ahead of fellow Briton Russell and Liam Lawson in the second Red Bull.
Franco Colapinto (Alpine), Oscar Piastri (McLaren), Arvid Lindblad (Racing Bulls) and Niko Hulkenberg (Audi) rounded out the top 10.
Seven-time world champion Lewis Hamilton, who had scored points in every race this season, missed out completely, retiring his Ferrari on lap seven because of brake failure.

George Russell was another big loser, with the Mercedes driver suffering badly from his team's decision to put him on two-stop strategy - the only one of the main runners to have this - which blew his chances of podium and left him even further behind his teammate in the title race.

articles.title: Kosgei wins Great North Run but McColgan withdraws
articles.summary: Kenya's Brigid Kosgei wins the women's race at the Great North Run as Eilish McColgan drops out early with injury, while American Zouhair Talbi wins the men's event.
body: Kenya's Brigid Kosgei achieved a convincing victory in the women's race at the Great North Run after Great Britain's Eilish McColgan withdrew with injury.
McColgan, 35, was continuing her return to racing after recovering from a broken toe, but she suffered a foot injury early in the half-marathon and limped off.
Kosgei, an Olympic silver medallist and former London marathon winner, eased to the win in one hour, six minutes and 15 seconds.
Despite that being slower than the course record of 1:04:28 she set seven years ago, Kosgei, 32, dominated from the start and ran much of the 13.1-mile race solo.

articles.title: Team Europe beat United States to reclaim Solheim Cup
articles.summary: Team Europe produced a dominant display in Sunday's decisive singles to beat the United States and claim back the Solheim Cup after a dramatic three days of see-sawing fortunes.
body: Playing in her first Solheim Cup, Lottie Woad held her nerve to drain the putt on the 17th green to give Europe an unassailable lead over the Americans and snatch back the trophy.
The putt sparked wild scenes on the green as Woad was mobbed by her fellow players, cheered on by a raucous crowd at the first Solheim Cup hosted in the Netherlands.
For only the seventh time, the teams came into Sunday's singles all-square at 8-8 after two nerve-jangling days at the Bernardus course.
But Europe started strongly in the head-to-head battles, inspired by England star Charley Hull, who put a miserable weekend behind her to win her match and clinch the first European point.

articles.title: Andy Roddick Reveals Serena Williams’ ‘Really Cool’ Gesture To Frances Tiafoe In Locker Room After US Open Heartbreak
articles.summary: Andy Roddick has revealed Serena Williams’ “really cool” gesture toward Frances Tiafoe in the locker room following his heartbreaking U.S. Open semifinal loss. Tiafoe enjoyed a strong run at the tournament, defeating Valentin Vacherot, Daniil Medvedev, and Alex Michelsen to reach the semifinals.
body: “The reason she was in there was to console Frances. That’s the reason she was in the locker room. It wasn’t just all fun good times and to crush me. She was in there to talk to Frances, which I thought was really cool of her,” said Roddick.

Williams also competed in the women’s and mixed doubles events at the U.S. Open. She partnered with her sister, Venus Williams, in women’s doubles, where they suffered a first-round exit. She then teamed up with Carlos Alcaraz in mixed doubles, with the pair reaching the quarterfinals before losing to Belinda Bencic and Flavio Cobolli.

The semifinal between Tiafoe and Shelton also marked a historic moment for Black tennis. The two Americans became the first Black American men to meet in a Grand Slam semifinal in the Open Era. By defeating Tiafoe, Shelton became the first Black American man to reach the U.S. Open final since Arthur Ashe in 1972.

After losing to Shelton in the U.S. Open semifinals, Frances Tiafoe spoke about the defeat during his post-match press conference. Praising his fellow American’s performance, he explained how difficult the match was.

articles.title: Antonelli wins Spanish GP after luckless Norris loses out
articles.summary: Kimi Antonelli took another step in his quest towards winning the 2026 world championship by benefitting from pit-stop misfortune for Lando Norris to win the first Spanish Grand Prix at the Madring.
body: McLaren's Norris had looked in control of the race after converting his superb pole position into a comfortable early race lead but the battle for victory turned on a lap-15 Virtual Safety Car when Aston Martin's Lance Stroll stopped in a run-off area.
With a VSC offering the field the chance of a so-called 'cheap' pit stop, McLaren were unable to pit Norris immediately as the Briton had just passed the pit-lane entry road.

But the following Antonelli and Verstappen had not, allowing Mercedes and Red Bull to pit their drivers respectively while Norris was running to a controlled reduced speed on track while marshals moved Stroll's car.

McLaren did pit Norris at the end of the next lap but, by then, the VSC had ended, meaning the field was back up to racing speed, with the misfortune then compounded by a slow seven-second service at his tyre change.

articles.title: CBF mourns death of former president Antônio Carlos Nunes
articles.summary: CBF vice president and the organization’s acting president on several occasions, Antônio Carlos Nunes, known as Colonel Nunes, has died at the age of 87 Credits: CBF. Antônio Carlos Nunes de Lima, better known as Colonel Nunes, died in the early hours of this Sunday (13), at the age of 87, in…
body: A reserve officer in the Military Police, he was born on November 21, 1938, in Monte Alegre, a city in the state of Pará where he also served as mayor.
A passionate Paysandu supporter, it was as a football executive that he made the greatest mark over the course of his career.

Nunes chaired the Pará Football Federation in different periods for nearly 20 years, was elected CBF vice president in December 2015, and served as acting president of Brazilian football’s governing body for several months in 2016 and 2021, and between 2017 and 2019.

“CBF mourns the passing of Colonel Nunes, whose story was marked by strengthening football in his home state of Pará and in Brazil. At this moment of profound pain and sadness, we express our condolences to his family and friends,” said CBF president Samir Xaud.
